patterns.line_granularity_column_blind: R90 #sg90a1 coverage.go (internal/coverage package, ADR-51573, shared by 15 perf linters via coverage.ShouldApply): hitCount(p,line) (coverage.go:103-111) matches on b.StartLine<=line<=b.EndLine ONLY - ShouldApply never passes or checks position.Column - so when 2+ coverage blocks span the same physical source line (e.g. a one-line if/else, or any gofmt-preserved multi-statement line), whichever block sorts last in p.Blocks silently overwrites count regardless of which block actually contains the diagnostic position. Distinct from presnapshot_position_blind (that class loses state across TIME/mutation order in a single flat map) and from branch_state_merge (that class conflates sibling if/else STATE within one function) - this class conflates sibling SPANS sharing one LINE NUMBER in an external coverage profile, a third kind of position-blindness. Currently fully latent: GH_AW_LINT_COVERAGE_PROFILE is never set in any CI workflow (confirmed via grep of .github, only referenced in SKILL.md docs) so ShouldApply always takes the permissive nil-index fallback - but per ADR-51573's own stated intent this is meant to activate eventually for all 15 gated linters at once. R91: the suggested findProfile follow-up was probed and filed separately, see suffix_match_nondeterministic below.
patterns.suffix_match_nondeterministic: R91 #sg91a1 coverage.go findProfile (coverage.go:81-98, same internal/coverage package as line_granularity_column_blind, never individually audited before): iterates idx.profiles (a Go map, randomized iteration order) and returns on the FIRST key satisfying a plain substring-suffix check (strings.HasSuffix(norm,'/'+normKey)), with no preference for the longest/most-specific match. Two files whose module-relative paths are in a suffix relationship (e.g. linters/foo.go vs pkg/linters/foo.go) could nondeterministically swap which profile block gets attributed to a query, purely as a function of map iteration order. A 4th distinct kind of position/attribution-blindness in this package (after branch_state_merge, presnapshot_position_blind, line_granularity_column_blind) - this one conflates two DIFFERENT FILES entirely rather than two spans/branches/times within one file. Distinct from the closed #52566/#52309 bug (findProfile previously never matched anything at all on a standard checkout - a false-negative no-op, fixed by adding the modulePrefix-stripped relative comparison that is itself the code now exhibiting this new wrong-match risk) and from the closed #53031 (unrelated mapclearloop body-vs-header gating fix, confirmed by R91 as correctly intentional, not a bug). No live colliding file pair found via Glob spot-checks of common basenames (types.go, config.go, registry.go) in the current tree - filed as a latent structural risk on the same reasoning-only basis as sg90a1 itself, not a confirmed live misattribution. PROBE further if a 16th gated linter or a second coverage-profile-key source (e.g. a different module) is ever introduced - that is when a real collision becomes most likely.
patterns.range_over_func_defer_semantics: R92 #sg92a1 deferinloop.go: isInsideLoop(69-83) classifies loop membership purely by AST node kind (ForStmt/RangeStmt/FuncLit via cur.Enclosing), never consulting pass.TypesInfo or rangeStmt.X's type. Since Go 1.23, ranging over a func value (iter.Seq-shaped) compiles the loop body to an implicit per-iteration function literal, so a defer inside it genuinely runs at the end of each iteration - the opposite of every other RangeStmt case and of this linter's own diagnostic text. Distinct from every other class in this file: those are about losing/merging/misreading STATE within an already-correctly-identified loop or branch; this one is about MISCLASSIFYING THE LOOP KIND ITSELF for want of type info, producing a false positive on a loop that was never the bug pattern at all. go.mod pins go 1.26.9 (fully capable); no live call site found yet (latent/forward-looking, same filing bar as sg90a1/sg91a1). PROBE any other AST-shape-only loop/scope classifier (ForStmt/RangeStmt treated as interchangeable) for the same blind spot if range-over-func adoption grows in this repo.
patterns.closure_var_alias_blind: R107 #sg107a2 goroutinemissingrecover.go run() (line 54): only flags `go func(){...}()` where Call.Fun unwraps to a literal *ast.FuncLit; `fn := func(){...}(); go fn()` resolves to a bare *ast.Ident and falls through the same exclusion meant for genuinely reusable named functions, even though the local closure is non-reusable and has no independent recovery. 4th linter hit by the broader alias/indirection-blind lineage (after reflectdeepequalusage function-value-alias, resourcetracker CleanupKey, goroutineresourceleak channel-usage). No live prod occurrence found (latent/forward-looking, same filing bar as sg90a1/91a1/92a1). PROBE any other goroutine/callback-launching linter (go/defer/callback registration) for the same direct-literal-only recognition gap.
patterns.presnapshot_position_blind: R79 #63768 lenstringzero: collectLenStringAliases builds ONE alias lookup map via a single whole-package ast.Inspect BEFORE run() analyzes any comparison, so the map holds only the FINAL state of each variable after all its later DEFINE/ASSIGN/IncDec/Range events have already been processed - not the state at each comparison's actual source position. Every comparison queries the same static post-collection map regardless of where it sits relative to a later mutation, so a variable aliased to len(s), used validly in an early comparison, and reassigned later in the same function has that early valid comparison retroactively blinded (false negative) even though it was correct at the time. Distinct from block_scope_state_reset (that class loses state too EARLY by resetting per nested block; this class keeps ONE state for too LONG - a single global snapshot with no per-position query at all) and from branch_state_merge (that class conflates sibling if/else branches within one flat map; this class conflates EARLIER and LATER source positions within a single linear scope). R80 #sg80a2 tolowerequalfold: collectCaseConvAliases (line 147) is structurally identical - one whole-file alias map built at line 41 before the separate BinaryExpr walk at line 47, with ASSIGN/IncDec/range-assign all deleting entries during the same collect pass, so an early valid ToLower/ToUpper alias comparison is blinded by a later same-scope reassignment. Confirms this is a recurring design flaw, not a one-off. R81: SWEEP COMPLETE on the remaining 4 candidates, ALL CLEAN. collectKnownPathConsts(hardcodedfilepath) collects package-scope CONSTANTS (fixed identity, immutable, immune by construction). collectPackageLevelSliceMapVars collects package-level VAR DECLARATIONS (fixed identity for the whole run, immune). seenmapbool's collectSeenMapCandidates/findNonSetMaps intentionally scans the whole function regardless of position since set-ness is a whole-lifetime property, not per-comparison-site - correct design. sprintfbool.collectSprintfBoolCandidates does a direct single-pass TypesInfo.TypeOf check, no alias pre-collection at all - immune. VEIN NOW EXHAUSTED at 2 confirmed instances (lenstringzero, tolowerequalfold); do not re-probe unless a new collect-then-query helper is added.
